cheat_sheet.title: Ethics, Authorization, Scope and Safe Labs — Structural Cheat Sheet
cheat_sheet.introduction: This sheet turns Ethics, Authorization, Scope and Safe Labs into visible relationships. It is a reference for planning, tracing, debugging, and explaining—not a list to memorize.
cheat_sheet.why_it_matters: The level contributes directly to a authorized assessment report for a fictional lab. Each concept helps the learner move from an ambiguous task to a contract, a representation, a verified transition, and an explainable result.

mental_model.summary: Represent the work as written scope, evidence chains, safe validation, risk ratings, and remediation before translating it into implementation details.
reasoning_cycle: Model variables, state, constraints, and relationships

input_questions: What may be absent or malformed?
output_questions: What shape and state are promised?

core_concepts.rule: Testing begins only after a named owner grants written permission for specific systems, dates, methods, and personnel.

core_concepts.title: Rules of engagement
core_concepts.rule: Rules define communication, permitted techniques, stop conditions, data handling, evidence retention, and escalation contacts.

core_concepts.rule: In-scope targets and actions are allowlisted sets; ambiguity, third-party ownership, or missing entries mean stop and clarify.

core_concepts.title: Isolated lab architecture
core_concepts.rule: A safe practice lab uses fictional data, isolated networking, disposable machines, snapshots, and no route to public targets.

core_concepts.title: Safety stop conditions
core_concepts.rule: Unexpected impact, sensitive data, unstable service, scope uncertainty, or lost monitoring triggers an immediate pause and notification.

core_concepts.title: Evidence handling and privacy
core_concepts.rule: Collect the minimum proof, timestamp it, protect integrity, restrict access, and remove it according to the agreed retention rule.

core_concepts.title: Risk communication without exaggeration
core_concepts.rule: Describe observable evidence, realistic preconditions, potential impact, uncertainty, and remediation without claiming unverified compromise.

core_concepts.title: Professional conduct and handoff
core_concepts.rule: Respect scope, minimize disruption, communicate promptly, and transfer findings through approved channels with clear ownership.

common_mistakes: Starting with syntax before defining the input-output contract.
Combining current state and a candidate update so rejection cannot be safe.
Treating an observed normal result as proof for every boundary.
Choosing a structure because it is familiar rather than because its operations match the constraints.
Ignoring empty, missing, duplicate, maximum-size, repeated, or out-of-order cases.
Hiding failures instead of representing loading, empty, rejected, and error states explicitly.
Optimizing before measuring the actual bottleneck or risk.
Explaining what the implementation does without explaining why its invariant proves correctness.
debugging_checklist: Can I restate the exact expected output?
Are input shape, units, identity, and trust level explicit?
Which state is allowed to change?
Which invariant should hold after every step?
What is the first observed step that differs from the expected trace?
Is the boundary inclusive or exclusive?
Can an invalid or repeated event mutate valid state?
Are asynchronous or external results stale, missing, or out of order?
Does the representation match the operation mix and constraints?
Did the repair pass the original failure and nearby regression cases?

lessons.title: Written authorization and legal boundaries
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Written authorization and legal boundaries within the isolated and fictional Aurora Practice Range.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Written authorization and legal boundaries to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Written authorization and legal boundaries is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Testing begins only after a named owner grants written permission for specific systems, dates, methods, and personnel.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Written authorization and legal boundaries, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use written scope, evidence chains, safe validation, risk ratings, and remediation. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Written authorization and legal boundaries
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: Testing begins only after a named owner grants written permission for specific systems, dates, methods, and personnel.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.
step_by_step_reasoning: Restate the problem as a testable input-output contract.
List state variables and separate current state from a candidate update.
Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.
Apply the structural rule for Written authorization and legal boundaries.
Trace the normal case one transition at a time.
Trace an exact boundary and one invalid case.
Compare observed output and preserved invariants with the contract.
Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

worked_examples.title: Normal case: contract to verified output
worked_examples.scenario: A learner applies Written authorization and legal boundaries while building the isolated and fictional Aurora Practice Range.
worked_examples.input: One well-formed input that satisfies the documented preconditions.
reasoning: Name the observable output before choosing an operation.
Represent only the state and relationships needed for that output.
Testing begins only after a named owner grants written permission for specific systems, dates, methods, and personnel.
Trace the transition and compare the result with the contract.
worked_examples.output: A valid state transition with the promised result and recorded evidence.

worked_examples.title: Boundary case: valid at the limit
worked_examples.scenario: The input is exactly at the smallest or largest documented valid boundary.
worked_examples.input: A boundary value explicitly included by the constraint.
reasoning: Write the inclusive or exclusive boundary symbolically.
Evaluate the predicate before changing state.
Apply the same rule used for ordinary valid input.
Verify that the output remains representable and accessible.
worked_examples.output: The boundary case is accepted once and produces a valid output without special hidden state.

worked_examples.title: Rejected case: preserve the invariant
worked_examples.scenario: An input violates one required relationship or arrives in an unsupported state.
worked_examples.input: An out-of-contract value paired with a previously valid state.
reasoning: Identify the failed constraint and stop before commit.
Keep the previous valid state unchanged.
Return a specific, non-sensitive explanation or recovery path.
Record the case as evidence for a regression check.
worked_examples.output: A controlled rejection, preserved prior state, and actionable feedback.

structured_representation.caption: A validate-before-commit trace for Written authorization and legal boundaries.

common_mistakes: Beginning implementation before defining the required output.
Changing state before the input or transition has been validated.
Memorizing the label 'Written authorization and legal boundaries' without applying its governing relationship.
Testing only one convenient normal case and assuming boundaries behave identically.
edge_cases: The smallest valid input or empty valid structure, when allowed.
The largest documented input, count, depth, size, or duration.
A duplicate, repeated event, retry, or already-completed transition.
Malformed, missing, stale, unauthorized, or otherwise out-of-contract input.
debugging_strategy: Freeze the first input that produces a wrong observable result.
Write the expected trace beside the observed trace.
Locate the first row where state, constraint, or output diverges.
Repair the rule or boundary responsible for that first divergence.
Rerun the failing case plus one normal, one boundary, and one rejection case.
progressive_hints: Label the input and promised output before naming any tool or syntax.
Separate current_state from next_state and write the validity predicate.
Apply this rule, then trace the boundary: Testing begins only after a named owner grants written permission for specific systems, dates, methods, and personnel.
lessons.summary: Written authorization and legal boundaries is mastered when the learner can model its inputs and state, apply the rule 'Testing begins only after a named owner grants written permission for specific systems, dates, methods, and personnel.', and prove the result with normal, boundary, and rejected traces.

lessons.title: Rules of engagement
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Rules of engagement within the isolated and fictional Aurora Practice Range.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Rules of engagement to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Rules of engagement is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Rules define communication, permitted techniques, stop conditions, data handling, evidence retention, and escalation contacts.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Rules of engagement, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use written scope, evidence chains, safe validation, risk ratings, and remediation. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Rules of engagement
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: Rules define communication, permitted techniques, stop conditions, data handling, evidence retention, and escalation contacts.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.
step_by_step_reasoning: Restate the problem as a testable input-output contract.
List state variables and separate current state from a candidate update.
Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.
Apply the structural rule for Rules of engagement.

Trace an exact boundary and one invalid case.
Compare observed output and preserved invariants with the contract.
Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

project.title: Ethics, Authorization, Scope and Safe Labs: Authorized Assessment Report For A Fictional Lab
project.real_world_context: A small team needs the isolated and fictional Aurora Practice Range that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate authorized assessment report for a fictional lab that demonstrates all eight skills from Ethics, Authorization, Scope and Safe Labs. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Testing begins only after a named owner grants written permission for specific systems, dates, methods, and personnel.
Rules define communication, permitted techniques, stop conditions, data handling, evidence retention, and escalation contacts.
In-scope targets and actions are allowlisted sets; ambiguity, third-party ownership, or missing entries mean stop and clarify.
A safe practice lab uses fictional data, isolated networking, disposable machines, snapshots, and no route to public targets.
Unexpected impact, sensitive data, unstable service, scope uncertainty, or lost monitoring triggers an immediate pause and notification.
Collect the minimum proof, timestamp it, protect integrity, restrict access, and remove it according to the agreed retention rule.
Describe observable evidence, realistic preconditions, potential impact, uncertainty, and remediation without claiming unverified compromise.
Respect scope, minimize disruption, communicate promptly, and transfer findings through approved channels with clear ownership.

constraints: Use only the languages, components, or structural interactions supported by the target application environment.

Record assumptions and unsupported cases explicitly.
The submitted result must be reproducible from the included instructions.

lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Metadata and information leakage within the isolated and fictional Aurora Practice Range.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Metadata and information leakage to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Metadata and information leakage is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Public or supplied metadata can reveal versions, paths, contacts, or structure; report only evidence within scope and minimize collected personal data.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Metadata and information leakage, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

lessons.title: Exposure prioritization
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Exposure prioritization within the isolated and fictional Aurora Practice Range.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Exposure prioritization to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Exposure prioritization is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Prioritize externally reachable, sensitive, high-impact, weakly controlled, and owner-unknown assets for defensive review.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Exposure prioritization, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use written scope, evidence chains, safe validation, risk ratings, and remediation. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Exposure prioritization
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: Prioritize externally reachable, sensitive, high-impact, weakly controlled, and owner-unknown assets for defensive review.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.

Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

project.title: Asset Discovery and Reconnaissance Concepts: Authorized Assessment Report For A Fictional Lab
project.real_world_context: A small team needs the isolated and fictional Aurora Practice Range that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate authorized assessment report for a fictional lab that demonstrates all eight skills from Asset Discovery and Reconnaissance Concepts. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Start from owner-provided inventory and record hostname, service, owner, purpose, environment, and scope status for fictional lab assets.
Passive review uses supplied records, while active checks send traffic; the authorization and impact profile differs.
Map only approved lab addresses to documented services and compare observed exposure with the intended architecture.
Public or supplied metadata can reveal versions, paths, contacts, or structure; report only evidence within scope and minimize collected personal data.
Place assets into zones and draw permitted data flows so unexpected pathways become review questions rather than exploitation attempts.
One signal may be stale or ambiguous; confidence increases when independent approved sources agree.
Prioritize externally reachable, sensitive, high-impact, weakly controlled, and owner-unknown assets for defensive review.
Turn inventory gaps and unintended exposure into asset ownership, closure, segmentation, and monitoring actions.

constraints: Use only the languages, components, or structural interactions supported by the target application environment.
Do not hide invalid input, unavailable data, or failure behind a successful-looking state.
Keep current valid state recoverable until a candidate transition passes validation.
Do not embed secrets, real credentials, personal data, or private endpoints.
Make all important output and error states accessible and testable.
Record assumptions and unsupported cases explicitly.
The submitted result must be reproducible from the included instructions.
Use only the fictional isolated lab and supplied fictional data.
No live target, public system, real account, harmful payload, persistence, evasion, credential capture, or destructive action is permitted.
Stop immediately when scope, ownership, monitoring, or impact is uncertain.

core_concepts.title: Finding versus verified vulnerability
core_concepts.rule: A tool finding is a hypothesis; safe validation confirms affected asset, condition, version, configuration, and evidence without harmful exploitation.

core_concepts.title: Scanner scope and safe configuration
core_concepts.rule: Limit a lab assessment by allowlisted targets, low-impact checks, rate, timing, credentials, exclusions, and stop monitoring.

core_concepts.rule: Corroborate results because imperfect detection can report absent weaknesses or miss present ones.

core_concepts.rule: Compare observed approved-lab facts with vendor or policy criteria while accounting for backports and compensating controls.

core_concepts.title: Risk rating with context
core_concepts.rule: Severity combines technical impact, exploit preconditions, exposure, asset value, existing controls, and confidence.

core_concepts.title: Minimal proof and non-destructive validation
core_concepts.rule: Collect the least evidence that demonstrates the condition; do not extract real data, alter state, bypass controls, or establish persistence.

core_concepts.title: Remediation selection and verification
core_concepts.rule: Prefer root-cause fixes, define compensating controls when needed, retest the exact condition, and document residual risk.

core_concepts.title: Assessment quality and reproducibility
core_concepts.rule: A finding records scope, time, environment, method class, evidence, assumptions, impact, fix, and safe retest steps.

common_mistakes: Starting with syntax before defining the input-output contract.
Combining current state and a candidate update so rejection cannot be safe.
Treating an observed normal result as proof for every boundary.
Choosing a structure because it is familiar rather than because its operations match the constraints.

lessons.title: Finding versus verified vulnerability
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Finding versus verified vulnerability within the isolated and fictional Aurora Practice Range.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Finding versus verified vulnerability to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Finding versus verified vulnerability is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. A tool finding is a hypothesis; safe validation confirms affected asset, condition, version, configuration, and evidence without harmful exploitation.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Finding versus verified vulnerability, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use written scope, evidence chains, safe validation, risk ratings, and remediation. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Finding versus verified vulnerability
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: A tool finding is a hypothesis; safe validation confirms affected asset, condition, version, configuration, and evidence without harmful exploitation.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.
step_by_step_reasoning: Restate the problem as a testable input-output contract.
List state variables and separate current state from a candidate update.
Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.
Apply the structural rule for Finding versus verified vulnerability.
Trace the normal case one transition at a time.

Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Compare observed approved-lab facts with vendor or policy criteria while accounting for backports and compensating controls.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Version and configuration evidence, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.body: Use written scope, evidence chains, safe validation, risk ratings, and remediation. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Version and configuration evidence
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: Compare observed approved-lab facts with vendor or policy criteria while accounting for backports and compensating controls.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.

List state variables and separate current state from a candidate update.
Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.

Compare observed output and preserved invariants with the contract.
Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

common_mistakes: Beginning implementation before defining the required output.

Testing only one convenient normal case and assuming boundaries behave identically.

Malformed, missing, stale, unauthorized, or otherwise out-of-contract input.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Minimal proof and non-destructive validation is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Collect the least evidence that demonstrates the condition; do not extract real data, alter state, bypass controls, or establish persistence.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure

For Minimal proof and non-destructive validation, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

project.title: Vulnerability Assessment and Safe Validation: Authorized Assessment Report For A Fictional Lab
project.real_world_context: A small team needs the isolated and fictional Aurora Practice Range that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate authorized assessment report for a fictional lab that demonstrates all eight skills from Vulnerability Assessment and Safe Validation. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: A tool finding is a hypothesis; safe validation confirms affected asset, condition, version, configuration, and evidence without harmful exploitation.
Limit a lab assessment by allowlisted targets, low-impact checks, rate, timing, credentials, exclusions, and stop monitoring.
Corroborate results because imperfect detection can report absent weaknesses or miss present ones.
Compare observed approved-lab facts with vendor or policy criteria while accounting for backports and compensating controls.
Severity combines technical impact, exploit preconditions, exposure, asset value, existing controls, and confidence.
Collect the least evidence that demonstrates the condition; do not extract real data, alter state, bypass controls, or establish persistence.
Prefer root-cause fixes, define compensating controls when needed, retest the exact condition, and document residual risk.
A finding records scope, time, environment, method class, evidence, assumptions, impact, fix, and safe retest steps.

constraints: Use only the languages, components, or structural interactions supported by the target application environment.

project.title: Sandbox-Only Web Security Testing: Authorized Assessment Report For A Fictional Lab
project.real_world_context: A small team needs the isolated and fictional Aurora Practice Range that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate authorized assessment report for a fictional lab that demonstrates all eight skills from Sandbox-Only Web Security Testing. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Within the isolated lab, map documented routes, methods, parameters, identity states, and expected responses without probing outside scope.
Use harmless boundary strings and schema cases to verify that the fictional lab accepts only intended shapes and lengths.
Build an actor-action-resource matrix and verify allowed and denied outcomes using only provided fictional accounts.
Inspect lab cookie flags, expiration, rotation, logout, and error behavior without attempting credential theft or session hijacking.
Compare supplied lab headers with the application's resource needs and recommend restrictive, testable policies.
Verify that fictional endpoints return consistent non-sensitive errors and bounded responses under approved low-rate tests.
Assess supplied manifests, lockfiles, build settings, and fictional advisories without executing untrusted packages.
Connect each safe lab observation to root cause, code or configuration control, regression test, and residual-risk statement.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Consistent risk rating is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Use a documented rubric and business context so similar evidence receives comparable priority and uncertainty remains visible.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Consistent risk rating, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

lessons.title: Metrics without misleading incentives
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Metrics without misleading incentives within the isolated and fictional Aurora Practice Range.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Metrics without misleading incentives to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Metrics without misleading incentives is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Track exposure age, verified closure, recurrence, and coverage rather than rewarding raw finding counts.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Metrics without misleading incentives, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

project.title: Professional Reporting, Risk Rating and Remediation: Authorized Assessment Report For A Fictional Lab
project.real_world_context: A small team needs the isolated and fictional Aurora Practice Range that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate authorized assessment report for a fictional lab that demonstrates all eight skills from Professional Reporting, Risk Rating and Remediation. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Executives need risk and decisions; technical owners need reproducible evidence, root cause, exact affected scope, and verification criteria.
A complete finding separates observation, preconditions, impact, likelihood, evidence, affected assets, remediation, and confidence.
Use a documented rubric and business context so similar evidence receives comparable priority and uncertainty remains visible.
Distinguish immediate containment, durable correction, compensating control, owner, dependency, cost, and target date.
Close a finding only when the agreed control is deployed, the original condition no longer holds, regression evidence passes, and residual risk is accepted.
Track exposure age, verified closure, recurrence, and coverage rather than rewarding raw finding counts.
Use authorized channels, protect details, allow coordinated remediation time, and follow legal and organizational requirements.
A professional portfolio links authorization, scope, methods, evidence, prioritized findings, remediation, retest, and lessons learned.

starter_materials.scaffold_policy: Level 5 supplies only constraints, acceptance criteria, and review checkpoints.

mandatory_features: Demonstrate Executive and technical audiences and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Finding anatomy and evidence quality and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Consistent risk rating and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Root cause and remediation options and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Retesting and closure criteria and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Metrics without misleading incentives and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Responsible disclosure and communication and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate End-to-end assessment portfolio and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
constraints: Use only the languages, components, or structural interactions supported by the target application environment.
Do not hide invalid input, unavailable data, or failure behind a successful-looking state.
Keep current valid state recoverable until a candidate transition passes validation.
Do not embed secrets, real credentials, personal data, or private endpoints.
Make all important output and error states accessible and testable.
Record assumptions and unsupported cases explicitly.
The submitted result must be reproducible from the included instructions.
Use only the fictional isolated lab and supplied fictional data.
No live target, public system, real account, harmful payload, persistence, evasion, credential capture, or destructive action is permitted.
Stop immediately when scope, ownership, monitoring, or impact is uncertain.

test_cases.expected: one correct output and valid next state

test_cases.condition: second valid input with different data

test_cases.expected: accepted only if contract includes it

test_cases.condition: valid retry after a controlled failure

maximum documented size
duplicate or retry
out-of-order or stale result
malformed or unauthorized input
debugging_checklist: Freeze a reproducible failing input.
Compare expected and observed traces.
Find the first divergent state.
Check the constraint at that transition.
Repair cause before symptoms.
Rerun the failure and adjacent cases.
Confirm state recovery and accessible feedback.
Record the limitation if the case remains unsupported.
completion_checklist: All eight level skills appear in the artifact or evidence.
The input-output contract is complete.
The structural model matches the implementation or decision flow.
All eight required test categories have evidence.
The rubric self-score totals 100 possible points.
No secret, real credential, or sensitive personal data is included.
Submission instructions reproduce the result.
Reflection names one failure, repair, and justified improvement.
submission_requirements: README with setup or review instructions

rubric.evidence: inputs, outputs, constraints, diagram, and milestones
mandatory behavior matches the project contract
clear responsibilities, transitions, and dependency boundaries
normal, boundary, invalid, repeated, and failure cases
usable states, safe handling, and recovery feedback
setup, decisions, limitations, evidence, and reproducible instructions
first divergence, repair, trade-off, and next iteration

common_failure_conditions: The result handles only one normal case.
State changes before validation.
A level skill is named but not demonstrated.
The diagram disagrees with the implemented flow.
A failed dependency leaves a false success state.
Submission evidence cannot be reproduced.
reflection_questions: Which assumption changed after the first trace?
Where did expected and observed state first diverge?
Which invariant prevented the most serious failure?
What trade-off did you make among clarity, cost, performance, accessibility, safety, or flexibility?
What evidence would you collect before a wider release?
optional_extensions: Add a second representation and compare which relationships become easier to inspect.
Add property-based or generated boundary cases without duplicating existing tests.
Measure one performance, quality, or risk indicator and justify an improvement threshold.
Design a migration or compatibility plan for one changed requirement.
project.acceptable_outcome_example: A submission may use the supplied contract and state templates, implement one complete primary journey, show all required failure states, and provide eight passing test records plus one documented limitation. The exact implementation remains the learner's work.
